tiles: Make.com scenarios tag, enrich, and route 800+ products automatically

LLM calls generate product copy, categories, and SEO fields
Python scripts rebuilt the Webflow export for GitHub Pages
challenge: An 800-product store with a fashion lookbook and an editorial magazine cannot be managed by hand — every new SKU would need photography, copy, categorization, and cross-linking across three connected sections. The real problem was not the design; it was that no small team could keep an inventory of that size accurate, on-brand, and shoppable without weeks of manual data entry per update.
approach: I built a Make.com pipeline (Make.com is a visual automation tool that chains services together) that watches a Notion database and routes each new product through a series of AI steps: an LLM writes the description, another tags category and collection, a third drafts SEO metadata, and the finished record is pushed into Webflow's CMS and the checkout system. Editors just update Notion — the pipeline handles the rest. When the site later moved to GitHub Pages, I wrote Python scripts to rewrite paths, fix nested directories, and keep the lookbook navigation intact.
result: Inventory updates that used to take hours now finish in minutes, and the site scaled to 800+ products without adding headcount. One editor in Notion runs what would normally need a small CMS team. The same pattern (Notion → Make.com → AI enrichment → CMS) has since become the template I reuse for other clients who need high-volume storefronts on a small-team budget.
skill_summary: Full-stack automation, Webflow CMS, Make.com workflows, Notion database management, Python scripting, and e-commerce architecture.

process.summary: Audit existing workflows, identify manual bottlenecks, and map where AI tooling or custom automation will deliver the highest leverage.
Build iteratively — custom scripts, AI-generated SERP descriptions, Webflow storefronts connected to inventory APIs. Ship early, validate with real traffic.
Monitor performance, A/B test conversion paths, continuously refine. The goal: a system that runs autonomously, not a one-time build.
